member.name: AnnouncementIsolation
member.para: The corpus geometry the thresholds sit in. Measured on "Corsa nello spazio" (build 244, 2026-08-05), replaying the guard over that run's own Analyze speech segments at each announcement's true onset: every one of the 65 chapters is flanked by about 3.0-3.9 s before and 1.0-2.2 s after, the number's own speech running 0.3-1.3 s. The false epilogue the same run wrote - Whisper heard "riepilogo" (Italian for "summary") mid-sentence and /epilogo/ matched inside it - measures 0.64 s before and 0.73 s after, on a 3.59 s stretch of continuous speech.
The failure this guard cannot catch. On the build-249 re-run of the same book, two marks left one sentence late passed the check honestly, at -92 dBFS.

The marks that would have failed at their written positions. Five of that run's marks, every one of them a mark left seconds late because refinement was broken (chapter 6 landed 2.2 s past its announcement, chapter 3 by 4.4 s); at their true onsets all five pass comfortably. That is why the guard is applied at the refined onset.

member.name: ForChapter
member.para: What a pause-only reading of the built-in phrases would have cost. Measured over sixteen books (469 marks, 2026-08-13), a pause alone would have dropped exactly one of them - "I Shall Wear Midnight" chapter 9, whose announcement follows the previous chapter's last words after 0.64 s against a threshold of 0.85 s - and that chapter is transcribed as a segment of its own, so it passes on the second route.

member.name: WithoutSatisfiedLeadIn
member.para: The one corpus mark whose pause falls short. "I Shall Wear Midnight" chapter 9, the one mark of the sixteen-book corpus with under 0.85 s in front of it (0.64 s), is transcribed as a segment of its own and passes on that.

Why a second route was added (2026-08-28). The segment-start route has a blind spot the sixteen-book corpus never showed: a book announcing a chapter as "<setting>. Chapter N." hands Whisper one segment holding both, so the match opens nothing, while the only pause it has is the one between banner and number. Both routes then fail together. Found across the Perry Rhodan Silber-Edition library (159 books), where 11 books announce chapters that way at some 17 positions; three lost a chapter to it outright and a fourth was saved only by a re-read that happened to frame the announcement differently. The punctuation route recovers all three and admits nothing else anywhere in the library - the measurement is in notes\Detection\PhraseMatching.xml under PrecededByPunctuation.

Why it is one helper rather than two. Until this change RegionProber.NamedIsolationFor carried its own copy of the waiver (if (match.OpensSegment) rule &= ~IsolationRule.LeadIn;). A prologue's ^ and a chapter's are the same ^, so the copies were an invitation for the two to drift; the named path now calls this.

member.name: IsolationRule.LeadIn
member.para: The corpus lead-ins. Measured over the fourteen-book corpus (2026-08-05): the twelve genuine prologue/epilogue/--custom marks all have at least 1.56 s in front, while two of them - Gruelfin's "Zeittafel" at 0.16 s and "I Shall Wear Midnight"'s epilogue at 0.44 s - have almost nothing behind.

member.name: IsolationRule.LeadOut
member.para: How many corpus marks have almost nothing behind them. Over the sixteen-book corpus, 17 of 469 marks have under 0.30 s behind them (2026-08-13) - a narrator running from the heading straight into the text.
